newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The new installation of a portable cricket pitch at the Melbourne Cricket Ground was endorsed yesterday by former Australian cricket captain Bill Lawry. The pitch was developed by StrathAyr and the Melbourne Cricket Club over the last 20 years. Page 20.

The American basketball star Todd Lichti is regarded as an outside chance of playing for the Perth Wildcats against the Adelaide 36ers in game one of their best-of-three National Basketball League quarter-final series tonight. Page 19.

For the second time this season rider Darryl McLellan will fill in for Glen Boss in a major horse race, this time in the A$500,000 Epsom Handicapp (1600m), which will be run at Randwick tomorrow. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Today is the judgment day for Australian Rugby League, as the Full Bench of the Federal Court will hand down its decision on the Super League appeal, deciding whether or not the ARL will rule league in this country until the year 2000. Page 40.

Eddie Thomson's six-year contract as the coach of the Australian Socceroos is about to come to an end and the key candidates for his replacement are John Kosmina, Frank Farina and David Ratcliffe, Zoran Matic and Raul Blanco. Page 40.

Captain of the Sydney Swans Paul Kelly has been awarded his team's best-and-fairest award. This is the third time Kelly has won the award and he won the vote by 34 hands, with a total of 270 votes. Page 39.
THE AGE

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor is uncertain whether he will be fit to play in the Test against India in Delhi next week, as he may not be fully rehabilitated from the back surgery he underwent last month. Page C8.

Billed Australia's biggest sporting event, the Australian Tennis Open, is having a hard time improving itself, because for the last few years it has kept getting bigger and better and this year expects all top 20 men and women tennis players in the world to attend. Page C6.

The AFL is confident its strong stance against any form of racism is working, with the reporting of two cases that arose from matches this season being mediated out of court. One incident involved a senior match and the other related to reserve grade players. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League has told Victorians it will no longer underwrite mergers for battling clubs, releasing a statement today which reveals it is withdrawing its A$6 million merger incentive, will only allow merger talks that have the full backing of its members, and that it will let clubs die rather than promote a merger which lacks the support of particular members. Page 1.

The Collingwood Warriors, a team created by a joint venture between Collingwood Football Club and Heidelberg Soccer Club, trained for the first time yesterday on Victoria Park. The team includes members like Socceroos Enrie Tapai and Goran Lozanovski. Pag 102.

Craig McDermott may never beat Dennis Lillee's record as Australia's most prolific Test wicket-taker, as he has been told his left knee will require surgery after he injured it during a club match on the Gold Coast last weekend. Page 102.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Sydney Kings beat the Canberra Cannons 113-89 in the first of the National Basketball League playoffs last night, and only require one more victory in Canberra on Saturday night to advance to the second round. Page 104.

Jockeys claiming there were divots the size of dinner plates filled with water refused to ride beyond the third race at Kyneton yesterday, in a move which will result in a dozens jockeys facing disciplinary action. Page 104.

Michelle Martin, the reigning champion of women's world squash, is flying out to defend her world crown at the annual World Women's Squash Championships in Kuala Lumper today. Martin says she is injury free and fresh from her win at the Australian Open. Page 102.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
